title: Tenant Quick-Glance micro-strip for Private Clusters
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Design a compact, horizontally stacked 'Quick-Glance' strip that appears at the top of a Tenant or Cluster page in the Private Console. The strip should give engineers and SREs a single-row summary of the most actionable signals: SLA exposure (latency/error risk), upgrade exposure (pending/failed nodes), recent networking anomalies (egress spikes, flaky peers), cost delta (24h), and one-click mitigations (roll back, throttle, open incident playbook).

Why: Private deployments demand concise situational awareness for tenants that are often managed by platform teams. Current Private Console pages require drilling into multiple dashboards to understand whether an upgrade or network event requires immediate action. This micro-strip aims to reduce decision-to-action time and lower cognitive load during incidents.

Scope: initial design will target desktop and compressed tablet widths; mobile will be a follow-up. The strip must be keyboard-navigable and meet WCAG contrast requirements. It should be implemented as a reusable UI component (design token-ready) that product and engineering can place on Tenant, Cluster, and Upgrade pages.
design_decisions:
- Use a fixed-height horizontal strip, max 56px, with five modular cards.
- Priority ordering: SLA exposure, upgrade exposure, network anomalies, recent errors, cost delta.
- Each module shows an icon, 1-line metric, and a micro-action (ellipsis or single CTA).
- Color semantics consistent with console palette: amber for warning, red for critical, blue for info, gray for healthy. Avoid saturated reds on non-critical surfaces.
- Telemetry hooks: quick_glance.view, quick_glance.click.module, quick_glance.action.invoke with module and tenant tags.
- Accessibility: modules must have aria-labels describing current state and action; ensure 4.5:1 text contrast for primary metrics.
- Performance: lazy-load detailed hover cards and only poll underlying signals at a 10s cadence when the tenant page is in focus.
acceptance_criteria: Component implemented as a single strip with five modules on Tenant and Cluster pages
Each module exposes the telemetry events and label keys documented in the spec
Micro-actions (roll back, open incident playbook, view traces) open the correct modal or route
UX tests: 5 SREs can interpret strip state and select correct mitigation in < 90s in a simulated incident
Accessibility: keyboard focus order logical, screen reader announces state and action, color contrast verified

Frontend: component skeleton, accessibility hooks, telemetry integration (ENG-PR #4321) - owner: Omar
Backend: expose aggregated quick-glance endpoint (ENG-2301) - owner: Priya; minimal shape: {state,module_metric,action_link}
SRE: run tabletop with patch cluster to validate micro-action rollbacks - owner: Lina
PM: prepare rollout plan and feature flag gating (canary) - Clara
review_notes:
PM feedback (Clara J): 'Love the single-row approach. Add an explicit 'confidence' small-dot for probabilistic signals (eg. predicted SLA breach). Please surface the time-range for the cost delta.'

Engineering feedback (Omar): 'Backend needs a lightweight aggregated endpoint to avoid multiple calls; prefer server-side aggregation every 10s. Also prefer module configs to be feature-flag driven.'

Design follow-up (Aisha): 'Iterate hover card to include quick links to traces and the last 3 deploys. Reduce icon weight for low-contrast environments.'

Action items from review: 1) Add confidence indicator (design). 2) Update telemetry spec with confidence field. 3) Backend schema doc draft and low-cost aggregator prototype (ENG-2301). 4) UX validation with platform SREs (schedule 2026-02-20).
